notes.calculus-section-17-1-32: The sine term is zero at both endpoints; either boundary fixes the cosine coefficient at 1, leaving the sine coefficient free.
notes.calculus-section-17-1-33: For λ<0 use real exponentials, and for λ=0 use a line; two zero endpoints force both coefficients to vanish. For λ>0, sin(√λ L)=0 supplies the discrete eigenvalues.
notes.calculus-section-17-1-34: For real roots their product c/a is positive and sum −b/a negative; for complex roots the common real part is negative. Even x e^(rx) decays when r<0.
notes.calculus-section-17-1-35: Write y=e^x(A cos x+B sin x). The endpoint matrix determinant is proportional to sin(b−a); when it vanishes the second row is a signed exponential multiple of the first.
